questions: Is GH #428 reproducible against the current dialect?
Phase 277 concluded it was not except in an ordering the corpus lacks. Is that right?
If a hash label in prose is matched, does any entry read a wrong value today?
Can the label-to-value span be tightened without losing legitimate forms?

findings.finding: Reproducible and live. docs/META_LEDGER.md entry #741 contains a backticked `**Previous Hash**` in narrative prose; PREV_HASH_RE matches it and hash_value returns the prose digest.

Harmless today only by ordering accident: entry #741 states its real field before the prose and readers take the first match. An entry whose narrative preceded its own field lines would return the prose digest.
Phase 277's probe measured entries carrying an inline value on a label line; a label quoted inside a sentence is not one of those, so its conclusion was broader than its measurement.
About 216 live entries put a code fence, a SHA256(...) formula or a bare newline between label and value, so the span cannot be tightened to 'value follows the colon'.
